t: 3158. Find the XOR of Numbers Which Appear Twice
o: Each value in `nums` appears once or twice; we must XOR together exactly the duplicated values. In example 1 only `1` repeats so the answer is 1; in example 3 both `1` and `2` repeat giving `1^2=3`; with no duplicates the answer is 0. Constraints are tiny (n, values ≤ 50), so any counting method works — even an O(n²) scan. The interesting part is doing it in one pass with O(1) extra structures.
k: A number appearing twice contributes itself once to the answer XOR; singles contribute nothing.
Toggling membership in a set detects duplicates in one pass.
XOR is self-inverse, so counting via XOR-friendly tricks is natural.

a.i: Count occurrences of every value with a hash map, then XOR all keys whose count equals 2. Direct translation of the definition.
s: Build a frequency map of nums.
Iterate entries; XOR key into answer when count == 2.
a.t: O(n) — one pass to count, one pass over distinct values

a.i: Keep a set of 'seen once' values. When a value appears again, remove it and XOR it into the answer. Values seen once never touch the answer, satisfying the requirement in a single pass.
s: For each x: if x is in the set, remove it and XOR it into the answer; otherwise add it.
a.t: O(n) — single pass with O(1) average set operations

w: Either approach is interview-ready; the set toggle is slightly more elegant and single-pass. Pitfall: forgetting that numbers appearing once must be excluded entirely (a plain XOR of everything would cancel duplicates instead of keeping them). Follow-up: solve with O(1) extra space — possible here by sorting or by using a boolean array of size 51 since values ≤ 50.
